Lukman, has postponed its second summit from Monday, November 23, to Monday, November 30, 2026, following requests by member parties.
The coalition said the postponement became necessary due to tight campaign schedules, as presidential candidates and their campaign teams were already engaged in demanding activities across the country ahead of the January 16, 2027 elections.
In a statement signed by Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, the Central Leadership Committee said it had approved the request to ensure the full participation of all member parties, presidential candidates and national chairmen.
“It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,” the committee said.
According to the statement, the November 30 date was agreed upon in consultation with key stakeholders to secure the widest possible participation.
To demonstrate their commitment to the coalition, all member parties have also agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on November 30 to enable their leaders to attend the summit.
The committee described the decision as a demonstration of the opposition parties’ willingness to put the collective interest of the country’s democracy above individual political ambitions.
“Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” it said.
The summit is expected to finalise and sign the coalition’s common agreement, as well as determine the direction of its activities ahead of the January 16, 2027 elections.
“We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the committee added.
The coalition thanked member parties, delegates and partners for their understanding and apologised for any inconvenience caused by the change in date.
It, however, noted that the venue and accreditation arrangements remained unchanged, adding that any further updates would be communicated to delegates and the media.
The Coalition for Democracy emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on August 31, 2026.
The multiparty platform was pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).
The coalition was established to implement the resolutions of the G100 Opposition Summit, with a commitment to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism and promoting free, fair, credible and competitive elections.
It also provides a framework for opposition parties to coordinate their activities, safeguard democratic institutions, uphold the rule of law and protect Nigerians’ fundamental right to freely choose their leaders.
Recall that the coalition, on Monday, disclosed that opposition parties are set to sign a “covenant for democratic renewal” at their second summit, scheduled for November 23 in Abuja.
Lukman, in a statement, said the opposition parties would adopt three foundational documents, including the national covenant for democratic renewal, the framework for opposition unity and the national reform programme.
He said the documents were developed by working groups drawn from participating political parties following the first summit of opposition leaders, held in Abuja on August 31.
He said the forthcoming summit would mark the next phase of efforts to build an opposition capable of defending Nigeria’s democracy, restoring public confidence in institutions and presenting citizens with a credible alternative for national leadership.
He said previous opposition cooperation had often relied on personal understandings that failed to survive changing political circumstances.
“This time, we have chosen to build on a different foundation. Opposition parties are putting their commitments in writing, institutionalising our cooperation, and establishing principles that must outlive both the moment and the personalities,” the statement reads.
